steps.title: Choose a bounded experiment
steps.explanation: Validate a fixed mode. Browser input cannot supply shell commands, filesystem paths, prompts or unlimited repetition counts.
steps.narration: Step 1. Validate a fixed mode. Browser input cannot supply shell commands, filesystem paths, prompts or unlimited repetition counts. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Declare cases and expected outcomes
steps.explanation: A case owns its prompt, grading kind, expected values and edit policy. Wrongexpected is a labelled negative control; its intentionally bad expectation is not a model hallucination.
steps.narration: Step 2. A case owns its prompt, grading kind, expected values and edit policy. Wrongexpected is a labelled negative control; its intentionally bad expectation is not a model hallucination. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Plan independent repetitions
steps.explanation: Repeated runs the same JSON case three times. Suite covers three different cases; Gate deliberately includes a failing outcome. One observed success is not a reliability claim.
steps.narration: Step 3. Repeated runs the same JSON case three times. Suite covers three different cases; Gate deliberately includes a failing outcome. One observed success is not a reliability claim. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Copy a fresh versioned fixture
steps.explanation: Copy the trusted fixture for every run and isolate the SDK home and config. Empty settings and temporary paths reduce shared state; they are not operating-system isolation or deterministic inference.
steps.narration: Step 4. Copy the trusted fixture for every run and isolate the SDK home and config. Empty settings and temporary paths reduce shared state; they are not operating-system isolation or deterministic inference. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Constrain reads and exact edits
steps.explanation: Resolve real paths before allowing known fixture reads. Fix mode admits only the reviewed average-empty-input change. The agent has no Bash or Write tool.

steps.title: Collect actual native results
steps.explanation: Consume the actual SDK stream and preserve its terminal result, requested tools and formatted text. A limit result remains a failure, even if a partial answer exists.
anchors: const run = query({ prompt: c.prompt, options });

steps.title: Run independent trusted tests
steps.explanation: Verify fixture contents first, remove the API key from the host test environment, then execute actual Node tests. Unchanged preserves the bug and must fail this outcome check.
steps.narration: Step 8. Verify fixture contents first, remove the API key from the host test environment, then execute actual Node tests. Unchanged preserves the bug and must fail this outcome check. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Grade output facts, not prose
steps.explanation: Parse the native structured_output with Zod, then compare project and count to the case expectation. Valid JSON shape is separate from factual correctness. Never grade by exact answer wording.
steps.narration: Step 9. Parse the native structured_output with Zod, then compare project and count to the case expectation. Valid JSON shape is separate from factual correctness. Never grade by exact answer wording. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Retain each completed run
steps.explanation: Append the actual graded record to JSONL immediately. Reports retain model, SDK, fixture and prompt provenance. Partial suites cannot pass the final gate.
anchors: const run = await runCase(caseId, emit, controller);

steps.title: Aggregate rates, cost and turns
steps.explanation: Compute measured averages from native result fields and retain measurement coverage. Missing metrics remain unknown. Wilson intervals show the uncertainty of tiny repeated samples.
steps.narration: Step 11. Compute measured averages from native result fields and retain measurement coverage. Missing metrics remain unknown. Wilson intervals show the uncertainty of tiny repeated samples. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Gate every case independently
steps.code:
const passed = groups.every((g) => g.passRate >= threshold);
  return {
    threshold,
    groups,
    passed,
    totalRuns: runs.length,
    passedRuns: runs.filter((r) => r.grade.pass).length,
    overallPassRate: runs.filter((r) => r.grade.pass).length / runs.length,
    pipelineExitCode: passed ? 0 : 1,
    interpretation:
steps.explanation: Require every case to reach the observed 80% threshold. A passing easy case cannot hide a failing case behind an overall average. Thresholds express application policy, not statistical proof.
steps.narration: Step 12. Require every case to reach the observed 80% threshold. A passing easy case cannot hide a failing case behind an overall average. Thresholds express application policy, not statistical proof. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Observe the real worker exit
steps.explanation: The parent observes the actual operating-system process close event and compares the exit code with the report. The UI shows both native outcomes and the case-level gate decision.
